source_text: Exhibit 10.18 MASTER SUPPLY AGREEMENT. MASTER SUPPLY AGREEMENT dated November 1, 2019 (the "Effective Date") between REYNOLDS CONSUMER PRODUCTS LLC ("Seller") and PACTIV LLC ("Buyer"). Seller and Buyer are referred to individually at times as a "Party" and collectively at times as the "Parties". Background: Seller sells various consumer and food service products, Buyer sells various products including products of the type made by Seller, and the Parties are entering into this Agreement to establish the terms and conditions under which Seller may agree to sell specific products to Buyer and Buyer may agree to purchase specific products from Seller for later resale by Buyer to its business customers. 1. Term. The Term commences on the Effective Date and ends on the earlier of: (a) the first anniversary of the expiration date of the last Purchase Schedule; (b) a termination date elected by a Party in written notice delivered any time after the expiration of the last Purchase Schedule; or (c) a termination date elected by a Party in written notice delivered as provided in Subsection 11(d). Rights and obligations survive with respect to products purchased and sold during the Term, products sold after the Term for orders accepted during the Term, Confidential Information disclosed or received during the Term, breach of this Agreement, related statements and omissions, Disputes, inventory Buyer is obligated to purchase under a Purchase Schedule, and provisions that expressly survive. 2. Scope. This Agreement applies to all products sold by Seller to Buyer and all products purchased by Buyer from Seller during the Term unless the Parties expressly agree otherwise in a separate written document signed by an officer of each Party. This Agreement will not require Seller to sell or Buyer to purchase any type or quantity of product except as expressly provided in a Purchase Schedule. A Purchase Schedule is a written supplement signed by an officer of each Party referencing this Agreement and identifying, among other terms, the specific products, quantities, specifications, commitment period, prices, price-adjustment mechanisms, and facilities at which products will be manufactured, stored and delivered. 3. Standard Operating Procedures. The Parties have been supplying select products to one another for approximately eight years and have been following Current SOPs covering forecasting, production planning, ordering, delivering and resolving claims. They will update business systems over the next six months and sign an amendment appending Updated SOPs. Until then they will continue following the Current SOPs. 4. Order and Priority of Interpretation. Conflicts are resolved in order of priority: first a Purchase Schedule for the specific products and duration it covers; second the SOP; third any Exhibit with respect to its subject matter; fourth the main body of the Agreement. 5. General Representations, Warranties and Covenants. Each Party represents, warrants and covenants on the Effective Date and during the Term that it is formed, registered, licensed and operating in compliance with Applicable Laws; is operating under a commercially reasonable code of ethics; may enter into and perform this Agreement without conflict or breach; is solvent and paying debts as due; and is not the subject of certain criminal matters. Each Party must promptly notify the other of changed circumstances. Actual, alleged or suspected non-compliance being investigated, contested or corrected in good faith and not materially adverse is not a breach. Non-compliance can be grounds to demand adequate assurances of performance under Section 2-609 of the Illinois Uniform Commercial Code, and a Party has ten days to provide adequate assurances acceptable in the other Party's good faith discretion. 6. Specific Product Warranties. Seller represents and warrants that each product sold at the time of delivery will be new, undamaged and unadulterated and free of defects in design, materials and manufacture, subject to certain Buyer-supplied intellectual property carveouts; manufactured and stored at approved facilities; manufactured, packaged, labelled, sold and delivered in compliance with Applicable Laws; compliant with written specifications; fit for the purpose of packaging, selling or use in consuming food subject to written qualifications and instructions; conveyed with good and marketable title free and clear of liens, encumbrances and claims arising by, through or under Seller; not infringe third-party intellectual property, subject to Buyer-supplied intellectual property carveouts; and comply with any additional representations and warranties in the applicable Purchase Schedule. Buyer's sole remedies for breach of warranty are rejection and return for refund, credit or replacement as provided in the SOP, reimbursement for certain recall or withdrawal expenses, and indemnification for any Indemnified Claim arising from the non-conforming product as provided in Section 7. 7. Indemnification. Defense and indemnification include payment or reimbursement of actual, reasonable, substantiated out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with investigation, defense and settlement of civil, criminal or administrative proceedings, and satisfying judgments, awards, orders, liens, levies, fines, penalties and other sanctions. Seller will defend and indemnify Buyer against third-party claims caused by actual or alleged breach by Seller, negligence or misconduct by Seller, infringement caused by products or Seller's related performance other than certain Buyer-owned licensed IP, governmental fines or sanctions caused by Seller's violation of Applicable Law, and any other matter Seller agrees to indemnify in a Purchase Schedule. Buyer has corresponding indemnity obligations for its own breach, negligence, misconduct, Buyer-owned licensed IP, Buyer-caused governmental fines or sanctions, and Purchase Schedule commitments. Tender, cooperation, control of defense, settlement rights, and special handling of conflicts of interest are addressed. 8. Insurance. During the Term each Party will maintain minimum insurance: Commercial General Liability Insurance with at least $10,000,000 per occurrence and in the aggregate and additional insured and waiver of subrogation endorsements; Automobile Liability Insurance with at least $10,000,000 per occurrence and in the aggregate and additional insured and waiver of subrogation endorsements; Workers' Compensation Liability Insurance in the minimum amount required by Applicable Law with alternate employer and waiver of subrogation endorsements; Employers' Liability Insurance with at least $10,000,000 per occurrence or greater limits required by Applicable Law; and Property Insurance providing all-risk coverage at replacement value. Insurers must have at least an A.M. Best rating of A-Minus VII. Insurance may be satisfied through primary and excess policies. Insurance must be primary and non-contributory with respect to the other Party's insurance for the insuring Party's negligence or other legal liability. On written request and before policy expiration, the insuring Party must provide certificates, declaration pages or binders, additional insured endorsements, alternate employer endorsements and waiver of subrogation endorsements. A Party may maintain deductibles allowed by law and may self-insure if allowed by law while maintaining tangible net worth in excess of $100 million USD and an adequately reserved professionally managed self-insurance program. 9. Limitations on Liability. Each Party disclaims all representations and warranties other than the express representations and warranties in this Agreement, acknowledges it has not relied on other representations and warranties, and waives claims based on them, subject to Buyer's entitlement to rely on descriptive transaction information and FDA guaranty letters and similar written assurances. A breaching Party is liable only for direct damages, and each Party waives consequential, incidental, indirect, exemplary, punitive and other indirect damages. These limitations do not limit liability for defense and indemnification of an Indemnified Claim, infringement on the other Party's intellectual property, unauthorized disclosure or use of Confidential Information, payment or reimbursement expressly required under the Agreement, or intentional misconduct in violation of Applicable Laws. Force Majeure excuses interruption or delay in performance caused by events outside the ability of the performing Party to foresee and avoid with commercially reasonable efforts, including natural disasters, war, terrorism, government action, accident, labor disputes, shortages, third-party acts, and fire or other casualty. The affected Party must promptly notify the other, provide requested information, and exercise commercially reasonable mitigation and recovery efforts. During and after Force Majeure, Seller must act in good faith in allocating available manufacturing capacity between Buyer and other customers. Buyer may cancel unfilled orders and procure from other sources until Seller recovers, and if interruption exceeds or is reasonably likely to exceed thirty days, Buyer may enter into longer term supply arrangements acceptable in its good faith discretion and need not resume buying until Seller recovers and those arrangements expire or can be ended without liability. This subsection does not excuse payment obligations or extend deadlines to exercise rights or remedies. 10. Confidential Information and Other Intellectual Property. The Parties anticipate exchanging Confidential Information over the Term for the Authorized Purpose. Confidential Information includes trade secrets and other non-public proprietary information requested and disclosed during the Term and designated or later described as confidential, subject to clear-and-convincing evidence fallback; information observed or heard in a plant, warehouse, facility or system of the Disclosing Party; the existence and terms of the Agreement; the existence, nature and extent of the business relationship; and pre-Effective Date Know-How of a Disclosing Party and its direct and indirect subsidiaries. Know-How means trade secret and other confidential proprietary information concerning manufacture, storage, packaging, marketing, sale and delivery of products. A Receiving Party and its direct and indirect subsidiaries may continue to use pre-Effective-Date Know-How in their possession for the Authorized Purpose and in connection with operation of their business. Nothing obligates a Party to disclose or license Know-How arising after the Effective Date. Exclusions from Confidential Information include public-domain information, pre-known information other than pre-Effective-Date Know-How, information from third parties without a confidentiality duty, information furnished to third parties without a confidentiality duty, independently developed information, and information that ceases to be protected without breach. A Receiving Party must safeguard Confidential Information, promptly notify the Disclosing Party of unauthorized disclosure or use, and cooperate in good faith to prevent it. Permitted disclosures include need-to-know disclosures to Representatives and Affiliates, disclosures to comply with law, disclosures in legal proceedings to enforce or interpret agreements or defend the Receiving Party, and disclosures and uses consented to in signed written notice. A Disclosing Party represents it owns and may disclose the Confidential Information, that the Receiving Party may use it for the Authorized Purpose and other limited purposes in the Agreement, and that the Disclosing Party will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Receiving Party and its Representatives against third-party IP claims arising from disclosure and use of that Confidential Information. Except for these limited representations and warranties, a Disclosing Party disclaims all other representations and warranties concerning its Confidential Information. Confidentiality obligations continue until the earlier of sixty months from disclosure or the date information ceases to be Confidential Information for non-trade-secret information, and until trade-secret information ceases to be a trade secret for trade-secret information. A Receiving Party must return or destroy Confidential Information within ten days of written request and after expiration or termination, subject to legal-retention and archived electronic copy carveouts. Except for limited disclosure and use rights and any license granted in a Purchase Schedule, the Agreement does not grant any right, title, interest or ownership in Confidential Information or other intellectual property. Any grant of right, title, interest or ownership in Confidential Information or intellectual property must be in writing and signed by the chief executive officers of the Parties. During the Term, a Party will not develop intellectual property for, on behalf of, or in collaboration with the other Party unless the Parties have entered into a Purchase Schedule or other separate written agreement signed by an officer of each Party. 11. Dispute Resolution. A Dispute is a claimed breach or other dispute over interpretation. The Parties will endeavor to resolve a Dispute through good faith negotiation for thirty days after notice before mediation or litigation. If unresolved, a Party may request JAMS mediation; the Parties will try to select a mediator within ten days, and mediation will be held in Lake County or Cook County, Illinois within thirty days in compliance with JAMS guidelines. Each Party bears its own costs and half the JAMS fees. If still unresolved, a Party may file litigation in a court of competent jurisdiction in the United States. For litigation involving only the Parties or their Affiliates, the Parties irrevocably consent to the exclusive personal jurisdiction and venue of the U.S. federal and Illinois state courts located in Lake County or Cook County, Illinois and their higher courts of appeal, waive inconvenient forum defenses, and waive jury trial rights. A Party may file litigation without negotiation or mediation for disputes involving intellectual property infringement, unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information, or requests for temporary restraining orders, injunctions or other equitable relief. Except as otherwise expressly limited, a Party may immediately exercise rights and remedies under Applicable Law upon a breach. A Party will not suspend performance under or terminate the Agreement or an accepted purchase order unless the other Party is in material breach and has refused or failed to cure within thirty days after written notice, and the Parties have been unable to resolve the related Dispute through negotiation or mediation or the breaching Party has refused or failed to attempt to do so. A Party may suspend performance or terminate immediately on written notice, without opportunity to cure or negotiation or mediation, for a material breach involving substantial harm to the reputation, goodwill and business of the non-breaching Party that cannot reasonably be avoided or fully redressed by an opportunity to cure. If Buyer fails to pay Seller by the invoice due date, Buyer owes the delinquent amount and a late fee equal to two percent of the delinquent amount for each full or partial calendar month it remains unpaid. If Seller prevails in litigation to collect, Buyer must reimburse Seller for actual, reasonable, substantiated out-of-pocket collection expenses. The late fee may not exceed the amount lawfully imposable under Applicable Law. 12. Miscellaneous. The Agreement and its Exhibits and Purchase Schedules entered into during the Term constitute the entire agreement and supersede prior and simultaneous representations, discussions, negotiations, letters, proposals, agreements and understandings, whether written or oral. The Agreement is not binding unless signed by the chief executive officers of each Party. No handwritten or other modification to the printed portions is binding. Amendments cannot be made through additional or different terms in quotations, purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading, letters, emails or other documents or communications, and no amendment is valid unless in writing and signed and exchanged by the chief executive officers of the Parties. Waivers must be in writing, signed by an officer of the waiving Party, and delivered to the other Party. The Agreement and all related claims are governed by the laws of the State of Illinois and the United States of America, without conflict-of-laws principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply. Invalid provisions do not affect the remainder. Assignment. This Agreement, its rights and obligations, is not assignable or transferable by either Party, in whole or in part, except with the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent will not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Either Party may transfer and assign the Agreement to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, consolidation or sale of assets without prior consent provided the assigning Party is not released or discharged from liability and the assignee expressly assumes all obligations. The assigning Party must give written notice before or promptly after the effective date of assignment. A change of control is deemed an assignment requiring consent, except that transfers or assignments that result in Reynolds Group Holdings Limited ceasing to control either Party do not require the other Party's consent. The restrictions do not preclude a Party from authorizing an Affiliate to purchase or sell a product on its behalf. Except as otherwise provided in a Purchase Schedule, there are no intended third-party beneficiaries. Except where sole and absolute discretion is expressly stated, a Party will exercise rights in good faith business judgment, perform obligations in a commercially reasonable manner consistent with industry practices and Applicable Law, and promptly take actions, provide information and sign documents reasonably requested by the other Party. Notices are effective on actual receipt, and emailed notices are effective only if acknowledged in a return notice. The relationship is one of independent contractors; nothing creates agency, partnership, joint venture, co-ownership or common undertaking. Except as may be provided in a Purchase Schedule, the Agreement does not create any form of exclusive supply relationship, and nothing obligates a Party to sell or purchase any specified volume, market share or minimum level of products during the Term. The Agreement includes rules of construction and may be executed in counterparts and accepted by email, mail or other commercially reasonable means showing the signatures of the chief executive officers of the Parties. In witness whereof, Seller and Buyer have executed this Master Supply Agreement as of the Effective Date. REYNOLDS CONSUMER PRODUCTS LLC, as Seller, by Lance Mitchell, Chief Executive Officer. PACTIV LLC, as Buyer, by John McGrath, Chief Executive Officer.
